*Applied Natural Language Processing — From Tokens to Agents*

## This version

This is a living book: chapters are revised as the field moves, and the Git
history is the full audit trail. Cite a **version**, not "the website" — the
prose you quote may have changed by the time your reader follows the link.

| | |
|---|---|
| Version | `v2026.09` |
| Chapters in this version | 39 of 39 and 6 appendices, in both English and Turkish |
| Language editions | English · Türkçe |
| Home | <https://bbardakk.github.io/uygulamali-dogal-dil-isleme/> |
| Source | <https://github.com/bbardakk/uygulamali-dogal-dil-isleme> |

## How to cite

Use the entry for the edition you actually read. The Turkish edition is a
separate edition, not a translation appendix, and has its own entry.

``` bibtex
@book{bardak2026applied,
  author    = {Bardak, Batuhan},
  title     = {Applied Natural Language Processing:
               From Tokens to Agents},
  year      = {2026},
  edition   = {v2026.09},
  publisher = {Published by the author},
  address   = {Ankara},
  url       = {https://bbardakk.github.io/uygulamali-dogal-dil-isleme/en/},
  urldate   = {2026-09-03}
}
```

APA 7:

> Bardak, B. (2026). *Applied natural language processing: From tokens to
> agents* (Version v2026.09). https://bbardakk.github.io/uygulamali-dogal-dil-isleme/en/

To cite one chapter rather than the whole book, use `@inbook` with the
chapter title and its stable URL — chapter URLs contain the chapter number,
so they change if a chapter is renumbered. The version field is what makes
your citation reproducible.

::: {.column-margin}
Include an access date. A living book has no single "published on" moment,
so the access date is the only thing that tells your reader which text you
saw.
:::

### Persistent identifiers {#persistent-identifiers}

A DOI is being registered through Zenodo, which mints one identifier per
released version plus a *concept DOI* that always resolves to the newest
one. When it exists, this page and `CITATION.cff` will carry it, and it is
the identifier you should prefer over the plain URL.

An ISBN has not been assigned. It identifies a published edition of a book
rather than a work, so it belongs to the PDF and EPUB editions rather than
to the website.

: Licenses {tbl-colwidths="[52,48]"}

Under CC BY 4.0 you may share and adapt the text, including commercially,
provided you give credit and indicate whether you made changes. Teaching
from it, translating it, and building a course on it are all allowed and
welcome; the citation above is the credit line.

Third-party material — datasets, model outputs, and quoted figures — stays
under its own terms, which the chapter that uses it names at the point of
use.

## Colophon

Written in [Quarto](https://quarto.org). Interactive figures are
[Observable JS](https://observablehq.com/plot) and run in the
reader's browser — there is no server, and no data leaves the page.
Static figures are hand-written SVG that follows the reader's light or dark
theme. Both editions build from one repository through GitHub Actions to
GitHub Pages.

Every number printed in this book was produced by running the code, on the
hardware named in each chapter's environment table, and re-checked against
the source before publication. Where a measurement failed to reproduce, or
came out against the expected result, the book says so.

## Disclaimer

The book is provided as-is, without warranty of any kind. Model behaviour,
library APIs, and published benchmark numbers all change; verify anything
you are about to depend on against your own data before you depend on it.
That is, in fact, the argument of the book.
